<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-1-weak-law-of-large-numbers" open>
<summary><span>Theorem 6.1 Weak Law of Large Numbers</span><span class="result-count">1 endpoint</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Y_i \in \mathbb{R}^k$ are i.i.d. and $\mathbb{E}\lVert Y \rVert \lt  \infty$, then $\bar{Y} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i \xrightarrow{p} \mathbb{E}[Y]$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendstoinmeasure-wlln">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.tendstoInMeasure_wlln</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Weak law of large numbers</strong> (Banach-valued, pairwise-independent form).</p>
<p>If <code>X : ℕ → Ω → E</code> is a sequence of pairwise-independent, identically distributed,
integrable <code>E</code>-valued random variables on a finite-measure space, then the sample
mean <code>(1/n) ∑_{i&lt;n} X i</code> converges in probability to <code>𝔼[X 0]</code>.</p>
<p>This is the direct composition of Mathlib's <code>strong_law_ae</code> with
<code>tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_ae</code>. Provided here as a named lemma to match the
econometrics literature's WLLN statement. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_4} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {E : Type u_5} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [inst_1 : NormedSpace Real E] [CompleteSpace E] [inst_3 : MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] (X : Nat → Ω → E),
  MeasureTheory.Integrable (X 0) μ →
    Pairwise (Function.onFun (fun x1 x2 =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun x1 x2 μ) X) →
      (∀ (i : Nat), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) →
        MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
          (fun n ω =&gt; instHSMul.hSMul (Real.instInv.inv n.cast) ((Finset.range n).sum fun i =&gt; X i ω)) Filter.atTop
          fun x =&gt; MeasureTheory.integral μ fun x =&gt; X 0 x</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean#L2858">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean:2858</a></p>
</div>
</details>
</div>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-2-transformed-wlln">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.2 transformed WLLN</span><span class="result-count">1 endpoint</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Y_i \in \mathbb{R}^k$ are i.i.d., $h : \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^q$, and $\mathbb{E}\lVert h(Y) \rVert \lt  \infty$, then $\hat{\mu} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n h(Y_i) \xrightarrow{p} \mu = \mathbb{E}[h(Y)]$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendstoinmeasure-transformed-wlln">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.tendstoInMeasure_transformed_wlln</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.2, transformed WLLN.</strong></p>
<p>If <code>X i</code> are pairwise-independent and identically distributed and <code>h (X 0)</code> is integrable,
then the sample mean of the transformed variables <code>h (X i)</code> converges in probability to
<code>𝔼[h (X 0)]</code>. This is the textbook transformed WLLN packaged as composition of the
Banach-valued WLLN with measurable-map preservation of independence and identical distribution. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_4} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {E : Type u_5} {F : Type u_6}
  [inst : MeasurableSpace E] [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_2 : NormedSpace Real F] [CompleteSpace F]
  [inst_4 : MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F] [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] (X : Nat → Ω → E) (h : E → F),
  Measurable h →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω =&gt; h (X 0 ω)) μ →
      Pairwise (Function.onFun (fun x1 x2 =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun x1 x2 μ) X) →
        (∀ (i : Nat), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) →
          MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
            (fun n ω =&gt; instHSMul.hSMul (Real.instInv.inv n.cast) ((Finset.range n).sum fun i =&gt; h (X i ω)))
            Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; MeasureTheory.integral μ fun x =&gt; (fun ω =&gt; h (X 0 ω)) x</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean#L2896">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean:2896</a></p>
</div>
</details>
</div>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="definition-6-3-consistency">
<summary><span>Definition 6.3 consistency</span><span class="result-count">1 endpoint</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>$\hat{\theta}$ is consistent for $\theta$ if $\hat{\theta} \xrightarrow{p} \theta$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-consistent">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">def</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.Consistent</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Definition 6.3, consistency.</strong></p>
<p>An estimator sequence is consistent for <code>θ</code> when it converges to the constant
limit <code>θ</code> in measure. This is a chapter-facing name for the Mathlib
<code>TendstoInMeasure</code> idiom used throughout the asymptotic files. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">{Ω : Type u_1} →
  {E : Type u_2} →
    {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} → [PseudoEMetricSpace E] → MeasureTheory.Measure Ω → (Nat → Ω → E) → E → Prop</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean#L33">HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean:33</a></p>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-3-multivariate-lindeberg-l-vy-clt">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.3 multivariate Lindeberg-Lévy CLT</span><span class="result-count">2 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Y_i \in \mathbb{R}^k$ are i.i.d. and $\mathbb{E}\lVert Y \rVert^2 \lt  \infty$, then $\sqrt{n}(\bar{Y} - \mu) \xrightarrow{d} N(0,V)$ where $\mu = \mathbb{E}[Y]$ and $V = \mathbb{E}[(Y-\mu)(Y-\mu)']$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-iidscalarclt-tendstoindistribution-gaussian">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.iidScalarCLT_tendstoInDistribution_gaussian</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.3, scalar iid CLT wrapper.</strong></p>
<p>For iid real random variables with finite second moment, the centered sample
sum scaled by <code>1 / sqrt n</code> converges in distribution to the Gaussian with the
matching variance. This is a chapter-facing name for Mathlib's scalar CLT. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ω&#x27; : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩ&#x27; : MeasurableSpace Ω&#x27;} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [inst : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω&#x27;}
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] {Y : Nat → Ω → Real} {Z : Ω&#x27; → Real},
  ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Z (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 (ProbabilityTheory.variance (Y 0) μ).toNNReal) ν →
    MeasureTheory.MemLp (Y 0) 2 μ →
      ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun Y μ →
        (∀ (i : Nat), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Y i) (Y 0) μ μ) →
          MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution
            (fun n ω =&gt;
              instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv n.cast.sqrt)
                (instHSub.hSub ((Finset.range n).sum fun i =&gt; Y i ω)
                  (instHMul.hMul n.cast (MeasureTheory.integral μ fun x =&gt; Y 0 x))))
            Filter.atTop Z (fun x =&gt; μ) ν</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean#L188">HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean:188</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-iidvectorclt-tendstoindistribution-multivariategaussian">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.iidVectorCLT_tendstoInDistribution_multivariateGaussian</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.3, finite-dimensional iid vector CLT.</strong></p>
<p>For iid <code>k</code>-vectors with finite second moment, the centered sample sum scaled
by <code>1 / sqrt n</code> converges in distribution to the centered multivariate Gaussian
with covariance matrix <code>covMat μ (Y 0)</code>. The theorem is stated in
<code>EuclideanSpace</code> form so it can be consumed directly by Cramer-Wold and Gaussian
law infrastructure. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {Y : Nat → Ω → k → Real},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp (Y 0) 2 μ →
    ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun Y μ →
      (∀ (i : Nat), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Y i) (Y 0) μ μ) →
        MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution
          (fun n ω =&gt;
            {
              ofLp :=
                instHSMul.hSMul (Real.instInv.inv n.cast.sqrt)
                  (instHSub.hSub ((Finset.range n).sum fun i =&gt; Y i ω)
                    (instHSMul.hSMul n.cast (HansenEconometrics.meanVec μ (Y 0)))) })
          Filter.atTop (fun z =&gt; z) (fun x =&gt; μ)
          (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 (HansenEconometrics.covMat μ (Y 0)))</code></pre>
</details>
<details class="dependency-list"><summary>Direct statement dependencies (2)</summary><ul><li><code>HansenEconometrics.covMat</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.meanVec</code></li></ul></details>
<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean#L253">HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean:253</a></p>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-4-multivariate-lindeberg-clt">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.4 multivariate Lindeberg CLT</span><span class="result-count">6 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Y_{ni}$ are independent with $\mathbb{E}[Y_{ni}] = 0$, variance matrices $V_{ni}$, $\nu_n^2 = \lambda_{\min}(V_n) \gt  0$, and the Lindeberg condition $\nu_n^{-2} \sum_i \mathbb{E}[\lVert Y_{ni} \rVert^2 1\{\lVert Y_{ni} \rVert^2 \ge \epsilon \nu_n^2\}] \to 0$, then $V_n^{-1/2} \sum_i Y_{ni} \xrightarrow{d} N(0,I_k)$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-multivariatelindebergclt-tendstoindistribution">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.multivariateLindebergCLT_tendstoInDistribution</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.4, multivariate Lindeberg CLT endpoint.</strong></p>
<p>Once scalar projection Lindeberg CLTs are available for a normalized triangular
array statistic, Cramér-Wold gives the corresponding multivariate Gaussian
limit. The textbook normalization <code>V_n^{-1/2} ∑ᵢ Y_{ni}</code> is represented by the
user-supplied statistic <code>T</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {T : Nat → Ω → k → Real}
  {S : Matrix k k Real},
  HansenEconometrics.MultivariateLindebergCLTConditions μ T S →
    MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution (fun n ω =&gt; { ofLp := T n ω }) Filter.atTop (fun z =&gt; z) (fun x =&gt; μ)
      (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 S)</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-5-heterogeneous-array-clt">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.5 heterogeneous-array CLT</span><span class="result-count">6 of 7 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Y_{ni}$ are independent with $\mathbb{E}[Y_{ni}] = 0$, $n^{-1}\sum_i V_{ni} \to V \gt  0$, and $\sup_{n,i} \mathbb{E}\lVert Y_{ni} \rVert^{2+\delta} \lt  \infty$ for some $\delta \gt  0$, then $\sqrt{n}\,\bar{Y} \xrightarrow{d} N(0,V)$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-heterogeneousarrayclt-tendstoindistribution">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.heterogeneousArrayCLT_tendstoInDistribution</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.5, heterogeneous-array CLT endpoint.</strong></p>
<p>This is the multivariate Cramér-Wold assembly for the heterogeneous-array CLT:
scalar projection CLTs for the normalized sample average imply convergence to
the centered Gaussian with covariance <code>V</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {T : Nat → Ω → k → Real}
  {V : Matrix k k Real},
  HansenEconometrics.HeterogeneousArrayCLTConditions μ T V →
    MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution (fun n ω =&gt; { ofLp := T n ω }) Filter.atTop (fun z =&gt; z) (fun x =&gt; μ)
      (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 V)</code></pre>
</details>

</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-sq-le-even-moment-div-threshold">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.sq_le_even_moment_div_threshold</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Even-moment Lyapunov tail bound for scalar triangular arrays.</p>
<p>On the tail event <code>c ≤ x^2</code>, the squared summand is bounded by the
<code>(2 + 2m)</code>-moment scaled by <code>c^m</code>. This is the deterministic scalar inequality
behind an even-moment Lyapunov discharge of Hansen's Lindeberg condition. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ (x c : Real) (m : Nat),
  Real.instLT.lt 0 c →
    Real.instLE.le c (instHPow.hPow x 2) →
      Real.instLE.le (instHPow.hPow x 2)
        (instHDiv.hDiv (instHPow.hPow (abs x) (instHAdd.hAdd 2 (instHMul.hMul 2 m))) (instHPow.hPow c m))</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean#L776">HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean:776</a></p>
</div>
</details>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Indicator form of <code>sq_le_even_moment_div_threshold</code>, matching the
Lindeberg tail summand. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ (x c : Real) (m : Nat),
  Real.instLT.lt 0 c →
    Real.instLE.le ((setOf fun y =&gt; Real.instLE.le c (instHPow.hPow y 2)).indicator (fun y =&gt; instHPow.hPow y 2) x)
      (instHDiv.hDiv (instHPow.hPow (abs x) (instHAdd.hAdd 2 (instHMul.hMul 2 m))) (instHPow.hPow c m))</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean#L797">HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean:797</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-integral-sq-tail-le-integral-even-moment-div-threshold">

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Expected-tail form of the even-moment Lyapunov bound. This is the scalar
estimate used to turn a higher even moment into a Lindeberg tail bound once the
array normalization supplies the threshold <code>c</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) (X : Ω → Real) (c : Real) (m : Nat),
  Real.instLT.lt 0 c →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable
        (fun ω =&gt; (setOf fun y =&gt; Real.instLE.le c (instHPow.hPow y 2)).indicator (fun y =&gt; instHPow.hPow y 2) (X ω))
        μ →
      MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω =&gt; instHPow.hPow (abs (X ω)) (instHAdd.hAdd 2 (instHMul.hMul 2 m))) μ →
        Real.instLE.le
          (MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt;
            (setOf fun y =&gt; Real.instLE.le c (instHPow.hPow y 2)).indicator (fun y =&gt; instHPow.hPow y 2) (X ω))
          (instHDiv.hDiv
            (MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt; instHPow.hPow (abs (X ω)) (instHAdd.hAdd 2 (instHMul.hMul 2 m)))
            (instHPow.hPow c m))</code></pre>
</details>

<div class="declaration-body">

    (∀ (i : ι),

            instHDiv.hDiv
              (MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt; instHPow.hPow (abs (X i ω)) (instHAdd.hAdd 2 (instHMul.hMul 2 m)))

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Additive CMT for <code>TendstoInMeasure</code>.</strong> If <code>f n →ₚ finf</code> and <code>g n →ₚ ginf</code>

  (∀ (n : Nat), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (f n) μ) →
    (∀ (n : Nat), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (g n) μ) →
      MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ f Filter.atTop finf →
        MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ g Filter.atTop ginf →
          MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n ω =&gt; instHAdd.hAdd (f n ω) (g n ω)) Filter.atTop fun ω =&gt;

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-7-continuous-mapping-theorem-in-distribution">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.7 Continuous Mapping Theorem in distribution</span><span class="result-count">3 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Z_n \xrightarrow{d} Z$ and $g$ is continuous $Z$-a.s., then $g(Z_n) \xrightarrow{d} g(Z)$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendstoindistribution-ae-continuous-comp">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.tendstoInDistribution_ae_continuous_comp</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.7, a.s.-continuity CMT in distribution.</strong></p>
<p>If <code>Xₙ ⇒ Z</code> and a measurable map <code>g</code> is continuous off a set with zero
limit-law probability, then <code>g(Xₙ) ⇒ g(Z)</code>.  This is the textbook
a.s.-continuity face of the continuous-mapping theorem; the null set is stated
on the law of <code>Z</code>, i.e. <code>(ν.map Z) D = 0</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_4} {Ω&#x27; : Type u_5} {E : Type u_6} {F : Type u_7} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩ&#x27; : MeasurableSpace Ω&#x27;}
  {P : Nat → MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst : ∀ (n : Nat), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (P n)]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω&#x27;} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] [inst_2 : TopologicalSpace E]
  [inst_3 : MeasurableSpace E] [inst_4 : OpensMeasurableSpace E] [HasOuterApproxClosed E] [inst_6 : TopologicalSpace F]
  [inst_7 : MeasurableSpace F] [inst_8 : BorelSpace F] {X : Nat → Ω → E} {Z : Ω&#x27; → E} {g : E → F},
  MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution X Filter.atTop Z P ν →
    Measurable g →
      ∀ {D : Set E},
        Eq (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe (MeasureTheory.Measure.map Z ν) D) 0 →
          (∀ (x : E), Not (Set.instMembership.mem D x) → ContinuousAt g x) →
            MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution (fun n ω =&gt; g (X n ω)) Filter.atTop (fun ω =&gt; g (Z ω)) P ν</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean#L221">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean:221</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-probabilitymeasure-tendsto-map-of-tendsto-of-ae-continuous">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.probabilityMeasure_tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_ae_continuous</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Push-forward CMT for maps continuous outside a limit-null set.</strong></p>
<p>If probability laws <code>νs</code> converge weakly to <code>ν</code>, and a measurable map <code>g</code> is
continuous away from a <code>ν</code>-null set <code>D</code>, then the push-forward laws converge
weakly.  This is the probability-measure core of Hansen's a.s.-continuity
continuous-mapping theorem.</p>
<p>The proof is the standard Portmanteau closed-set argument: for closed <code>C</code>, the
closure of <code>g ⁻¹' C</code> is contained in <code>g ⁻¹' C ∪ D</code>; weak convergence controls
the closed closure, and the null set removes the discontinuity contribution. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {ι : Type u_4} {E : Type u_5} {F : Type u_6} {L : Filter ι} [L.IsCountablyGenerated] [inst : TopologicalSpace E]
  [inst_1 : MeasurableSpace E] [inst_2 : OpensMeasurableSpace E] [HasOuterApproxClosed E] [inst_4 : TopologicalSpace F]
  [inst_5 : MeasurableSpace F] [inst_6 : BorelSpace F] {νs : ι → MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure E}
  {ν : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure E},
  Filter.Tendsto νs L (nhds ν) →
    ∀ {g : E → F} (hg : Measurable g) {D : Set E},
      Eq (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe ν.toMeasure D) 0 →
        (∀ (x : E), Not (Set.instMembership.mem D x) → ContinuousAt g x) →
          Filter.Tendsto (fun i =&gt; (νs i).map ⋯) L (nhds (ν.map ⋯))</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean#L161">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean:161</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendstoindistribution-continuous-comp">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.tendstoInDistribution_continuous_comp</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.7, global continuous-mapping theorem in distribution.</strong></p>
<p>If <code>Xₙ ⇒ Z</code> and <code>g</code> is globally continuous, then <code>g(Xₙ) ⇒ g(Z)</code>. This is the
Mathlib-backed global-continuity face of Hansen's distributional CMT; see
<code>tendstoInDistribution_ae_continuous_comp</code> for the textbook a.s.-continuity
form. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_4} {Ω&#x27; : Type u_5} {E : Type u_6} {F : Type u_7} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩ&#x27; : MeasurableSpace Ω&#x27;}
  {P : Nat → MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst : ∀ (n : Nat), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (P n)]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω&#x27;} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] [inst_2 : TopologicalSpace E]
  [inst_3 : MeasurableSpace E] [inst_4 : OpensMeasurableSpace E] [inst_5 : TopologicalSpace F]
  [inst_6 : MeasurableSpace F] [inst_7 : BorelSpace F] {X : Nat → Ω → E} {Z : Ω&#x27; → E} {g : E → F},
  MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution X Filter.atTop Z P ν →
    Continuous g → MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution (fun n ω =&gt; g (X n ω)) Filter.atTop (fun ω =&gt; g (Z ω)) P ν</code></pre>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-8-delta-method">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.8 Delta Method</span><span class="result-count">6 of 7 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $p_n(\hat{\mu} - \mu) \xrightarrow{d} \xi$ and $g$ is continuously differentiable near $\mu$, then $p_n(g(\hat{\mu}) - g(\mu)) \xrightarrow{d} G' \xi$ where $G = \partial g(\mu)'/\partial u$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-deltamethod-remainder-islittleo">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.deltaMethod_remainder_isLittleO</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Deterministic Delta-method remainder from Mathlib's Fréchet derivative API.</p>
<p>This is the analytic core of Hansen Theorem 6.8: after subtracting the linear
approximation, the remainder is little-o of the input displacement. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {E : Type u_3} {F : Type u_4} [inst : SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace Real E]
  [inst_2 : SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_3 : NormedSpace Real F] {g : E → F}
  {G : ContinuousLinearMap (RingHom.id Real) E F} {θ : E},
  HasFDerivAt g G θ →
    Asymptotics.IsLittleO (nhds θ)
      (fun x =&gt; instHSub.hSub (instHSub.hSub (g x) (g θ)) (ContinuousLinearMap.funLike.coe G (instHSub.hSub x θ)))
      fun x =&gt; instHSub.hSub x θ</code></pre>
</details>

</div>
</details>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Delta-method Slutsky wrapper.</p>
<p>If the linearized statistic <code>Tₙ</code> converges in distribution and the nonlinear
statistic differs from <code>G Tₙ</code> by an <code>oₚ(1)</code> remainder, then the nonlinear
statistic has the linear image of the limit.  The deterministic source of the
remainder is <code>deltaMethod_remainder_isLittleO</code>. </p></div>

<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ω&#x27; : Type u_2} {E : Type u_3} {F : Type u_4} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩ&#x27; : MeasurableSpace Ω&#x27;}
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω&#x27;} [inst : SeminormedAddCommGroup E]
  [inst_1 : NormedSpace Real E] [inst_2 : MeasurableSpace E] [inst_3 : BorelSpace E] [inst_4 : SeminormedAddCommGroup F]
  [inst_5 : NormedSpace Real F] [SecondCountableTopology F] [inst_7 : MeasurableSpace F] [inst_8 : BorelSpace F]
  [inst_9 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [inst_10 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] {T : Nat → Ω → E}
  {Z : Ω&#x27; → E} {R : Nat → Ω → F} {G : ContinuousLinearMap (RingHom.id Real) E F},
  MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution T Filter.atTop Z (fun x =&gt; μ) ν →
    (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ R Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; 0) →
      (∀ (n : Nat), AEMeasurable (R n) μ) →
        MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution
          (fun n ω =&gt; instHAdd.hAdd (ContinuousLinearMap.funLike.coe G (T n ω)) (R n ω)) Filter.atTop
          (fun ω =&gt; ContinuousLinearMap.funLike.coe G (Z ω)) (fun x =&gt; μ) ν</code></pre>
</details>

<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Y_i \in \mathbb{R}^m$ are i.i.d., $h : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^k$, $\mathbb{E}\lVert h(Y) \rVert \lt  \infty$, and $g : \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^q$ is continuous at $\mu$, then $\hat{\theta} \xrightarrow{p} \theta$</p></div>

<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Measurable-space compatibility form of the local continuous mapping theorem.</strong></p>
<p>If <code>f n →ₚ x</code> and <code>h</code> is continuous at <code>x</code>, then <code>h (f n) →ₚ h x</code>, provided
the input and composed sequences are a.e. strongly measurable.  The stronger
metric-space theorem

when those technical premises are not part of the mathematical statement. </p></div>

<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Y_i \in \mathbb{R}^m$ are i.i.d., $\mathbb{E}\lVert h(Y) \rVert^2 \lt  \infty$, and $g$ is continuously differentiable near $\mu$, then $\sqrt{n}(\hat{\theta} - \theta) \xrightarrow{d} N(0,V_\theta)$ where $V_\theta = G' V G$</p></div>

<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 6.10, Gaussian Delta-method wrapper.</p>
<p>The input statistic converges to a centered multivariate Gaussian.  The nonlinear
statistic is represented as its matrix-linear Delta-method image plus an

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-11-best-unbiased-estimation-of-the-mean">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.11 best unbiased estimation of the mean</span><span class="result-count">6 of 10 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $\tilde{\mu}$ is unbiased for $\mu = \mathbb{E}[h(Y)]$ and $\mathbb{E}\lVert h(Y) \rVert^2 \lt  \infty$, then $\operatorname{Var}(\tilde{\mu}) \ge n^{-1} V$ where $V = \mathbb{E}[(h(Y)-\mu)(h(Y)-\mu)']$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-iidsamplemean-covmat-eq-inv-card-smul">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.iidSampleMean_covMat_eq_inv_card_smul</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.11, covariance-matrix sample-mean sharpness face.</strong></p>
<p>For finite-dimensional square-integrable observations whose coordinates are
pairwise independent across distinct observations and whose one-draw covariance
matrix is common across observations, the covariance matrix of the sample mean
is exactly <code>1 / n</code> times that one-draw covariance matrix. This is the
matrix-valued version of the sample-mean sharpness identity around Hansen's
best-unbiased-estimation theorem. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {k : Type u_3}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [inst : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {Z : ι → Ω → k → Real} (j : ι),
  (∀ (i : ι) (a : k), MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun ω =&gt; Z i ω a) 2 μ) →
    (∀ (a b : k), Pairwise fun i l =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (fun ω =&gt; Z i ω a) (fun ω =&gt; Z l ω b) μ) →
      (∀ (i : ι) (a b : k),

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-iidsamplemean-variance-eq-inv-card-mul">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.iidSampleMean_variance_eq_inv_card_mul</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.11, sample-mean sharpness face.</strong></p>
<p>For pairwise independent identically distributed square-integrable scalar
observations, the variance of the finite-sample average is <code>1 / n</code> times the
variance of one draw. This formalizes the sharp sample-mean variance identity
around Hansen's best-unbiased-estimation theorem; the full lower bound for
arbitrary unbiased estimators is a separate efficiency statement. </p></div>

<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [inst : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {Z : ι → Ω → Real} (j : ι),
  (∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.MemLp (Z i) 2 μ) →
    (Pairwise fun i j =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (Z i) (Z j) μ) →
      (∀ (i : ι), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z i) (Z j) μ μ) →
        Eq
          (ProbabilityTheory.variance
            (fun ω =&gt; instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast) (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt; Z i ω)) μ)
          (instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast) (ProbabilityTheory.variance (Z j) μ))</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-iidlinearunbiasedestimator-variance-ge-samplemean">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.iidLinearUnbiasedEstimator_variance_ge_sampleMean</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.11, scalar best-linear-unbiased face.</strong></p>
<p>Among linear unbiased estimators <code>∑ᵢ wᵢ Zᵢ</code> with weights summing to one, the
equal-weight sample mean has minimal variance under iid square-integrable scalar
observations. This is a linear-estimator lower-bound face of Hansen's
best-unbiased-estimation theorem; the arbitrary-estimator lower bound remains a
separate efficiency statement. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [inst : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {Z : ι → Ω → Real} (j : ι) (w : ι → Real),
  (∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.MemLp (Z i) 2 μ) →
    (Pairwise fun i l =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (Z i) (Z l) μ) →
      (∀ (i : ι), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z i) (Z j) μ μ) →
        Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt; w i) 1 →
          Real.instLE.le (instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast) (ProbabilityTheory.variance (Z j) μ))
            (ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun ω =&gt; Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt; instHMul.hMul (w i) (Z i ω)) μ)</code></pre>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-iidlinearunbiasedestimator-covmat-sub-samplemean-possemidef">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.iidLinearUnbiasedEstimator_covMat_sub_sampleMean_posSemidef</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.11, vector best-linear-unbiased face.</strong></p>
<p>For scalar weights summing to one, the covariance matrix of the weighted linear
estimator <code>∑ᵢ wᵢ Zᵢ</code> dominates the covariance matrix of the equal-weight sample
mean. The proof applies the scalar best-linear-unbiased theorem to every fixed
linear projection and then repackages the result as a positive-semidefinite
matrix inequality. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {k : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype k]
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {Z : ι → Ω → k → Real} (j : ι)
  (w : ι → Real),
  (∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.MemLp (Z i) 2 μ) →
    (Pairwise fun i l =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (Z i) (Z l) μ) →
      (∀ (i : ι), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z i) (Z j) μ μ) →
        Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt; w i) 1 →

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-iidestimator-variance-ge-samplemean-of-mean-add-uncorrelated">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.iidEstimator_variance_ge_sampleMean_of_mean_add_uncorrelated</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.11, scalar orthogonal-residual efficiency face.</strong></p>
<p>If a square-integrable scalar estimator decomposes into the sample mean plus a
residual that is uncorrelated with the sample mean, then its variance dominates
the sample-mean variance <code>n⁻¹ Var[Z_j]</code>. This composes the sharp sample-mean
variance identity with the orthogonal-residual variance algebra; the remaining
arbitrary-estimator task is to derive this orthogonality from a theorem-facing
unbiasedness/completeness condition. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [inst : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {Z : ι → Ω → Real} {T R : Ω → Real} (j : ι),
  (∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.MemLp (Z i) 2 μ) →
    (Pairwise fun i l =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (Z i) (Z l) μ) →
      (∀ (i : ι), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z i) (Z j) μ μ) →
        MeasureTheory.MemLp R 2 μ →
          (∀ (ω : Ω),
              Eq (T ω)
                (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast) (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt; Z i ω))
                  (R ω))) →
            Eq
                (ProbabilityTheory.covariance
                  (fun ω =&gt; instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast) (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt; Z i ω)) R
                  μ)
                0 →
              Real.instLE.le
                (instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast) (ProbabilityTheory.variance (Z j) μ))
                (ProbabilityTheory.variance T μ)</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean#L694">HansenEconometrics/Chapter6Asymptotics.lean:694</a></p>
</div>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-iidestimator-covmat-sub-samplemean-possemidef-of-mean-add-uncorrelated">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.iidEstimator_covMat_sub_sampleMean_posSemidef_of_mean_add_uncorrelated</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.11, vector orthogonal-residual efficiency face.</strong></p>
<p>If a finite-dimensional estimator decomposes into the vector sample mean plus a
square-integrable residual whose every linear projection is uncorrelated with
the corresponding sample-mean projection, then its covariance matrix dominates
<code>n⁻¹ covMat(Z_j)</code> in positive-semidefinite order. This is the vector form of the
orthogonal-residual route to Hansen's best-unbiased-estimation bound. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {k : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype k]
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {Z : ι → Ω → k → Real} {T R : Ω → k → Real}
  (j : ι),
  (∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.MemLp (Z i) 2 μ) →
    (∀ (a b : k), Pairwise fun i l =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (fun ω =&gt; Z i ω a) (fun ω =&gt; Z l ω b) μ) →
      (∀ (i : ι), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z i) (Z j) μ μ) →
        MeasureTheory.MemLp R 2 μ →
          (∀ (ω : Ω),
              Eq (T ω)
                (instHAdd.hAdd
                  (fun a =&gt; instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast) (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt; Z i ω a))
                  (R ω))) →
            (∀ (a : k → Real),
                Eq
                  (ProbabilityTheory.covariance
                    (fun ω =&gt;
                      dotProduct
                        (fun b =&gt;
                          instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast) (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt; Z i ω b))
                        a)
                    (fun ω =&gt; dotProduct (R ω) a) μ)
                  0) →
              (instHSub.hSub (HansenEconometrics.covMat μ T)
                  (instHSMul.hSMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast)
                    (HansenEconometrics.covMat μ (Z j)))).PosSemidef</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-12-moment-bound-implies-stochastic-boundedness">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.12 moment bound implies stochastic boundedness</span><span class="result-count">6 of 14 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $\mathbb{E}\lVert Z_n \rVert^\delta = O(a_n)$ for some $\delta \gt  0$, then $Z_n = O_p(a_n^{1/\delta})$; if $\mathbb{E}\lVert Z_n \rVert^\delta = o(a_n)$, then $Z_n = o_p(a_n^{1/\delta})$</p></div>

      Filter.Eventually (fun n =&gt; Real.instLE.le (MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt; Real.norm.norm (X n ω)) C)

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-13-bounded-first-moments-pass-to-the-limit">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.13 bounded first moments pass to the limit</span><span class="result-count">6 of 7 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Z_n \xrightarrow{d} Z$ and $\mathbb{E}\lVert Z_n \rVert \le C$, then $\mathbb{E}\lVert Z \rVert \le C$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-elpnorm-one-limit-le-of-tendstoinmeasure-bound">

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.13, convergence-in-measure bounded-moment wrapper.</strong></p>
<p>If a real sequence converges in measure and has eventually bounded <code>L¹</code>
seminorm, the limit has the same <code>L¹</code> bound. This is the
convergence-in-measure face of Hansen's bounded-first-moment passage to the
limit; the textbook weak-convergence statement is stronger. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {α : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {Z : Nat → α → Real} {Zlim : α → Real}
  {C : ENNReal},
  Filter.Eventually (fun n =&gt; ENNReal.instPartialOrder.le (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (Z n) 1 μ) C) Filter.atTop →
    MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ Z Filter.atTop Zlim →
      (∀ (n : Nat), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (Z n) μ) →
        ENNReal.instPartialOrder.le (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm Zlim 1 μ) C</code></pre>
</details>

</div>

<details class="result-group" id="definition-6-4-uniform-integrability">
<summary><span>Definition 6.4 uniform integrability</span><span class="result-count">3 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>$Z_n$ is uniformly integrable if $\lim_{M \to \infty} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{E}[\lVert Z_n \rVert 1\{\lVert Z_n \rVert \gt  M\}] = 0$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-uniformintegrable-tail-elpnorm-one">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.uniformIntegrable_tail_eLpNorm_one</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Uniform integrability gives uniform control of large-tail <code>L¹</code> seminorms.</p>
<p>This is the Mathlib-backed UI layer used by Hansen Theorem 6.16.  The result is
for a real-valued sequence <code>Z</code>; in the textbook application <code>Z i</code> is the
nonnegative power variable <code>|Y_i|^r</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Z : Nat → Ω → Real},
  MeasureTheory.UniformIntegrable Z 1 μ →
    ∀ {ε : Real},
      Real.instLT.lt 0 ε →
        Exists fun C =&gt;
          ∀ (i : Nat),
            ENNReal.instPartialOrder.le
              (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm
                ((setOf fun ω =&gt; NNReal.instPartialOrder.le C (SeminormedAddGroup.toNNNorm.nnnorm (Z i ω))).indicator
                  (Z i))
                1 μ)
              (ENNReal.ofReal ε)</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean#L37">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean:37</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-uniformintegrable-one-of-tail-elpnorm">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.uniformIntegrable_one_of_tail_eLpNorm</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Tail <code>L¹</code> control gives Mathlib's probability-theory uniform integrability.</p>
<p>This is the converse of <code>uniformIntegrable_tail_eLpNorm_one</code>, stated as a
chapter-facing Definition 6.4 bridge. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {Z : Nat → Ω → Real},
  (∀ (i : Nat), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (Z i) μ) →
    (∀ (ε : Real),
        Real.instLT.lt 0 ε →
          Exists fun C =&gt;
            ∀ (i : Nat),
              ENNReal.instPartialOrder.le
                (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm
                  ((setOf fun ω =&gt; NNReal.instPartialOrder.le C (SeminormedAddGroup.toNNNorm.nnnorm (Z i ω))).indicator
                    (Z i))
                  1 μ)
                (ENNReal.ofReal ε)) →
      MeasureTheory.UniformIntegrable Z 1 μ</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean#L50">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean:50</a></p>
</div>
</details>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Two-sided tail characterization of <code>L¹</code> uniform integrability for real

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-14-primitive-condition-for-uniform-integrability">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.14 primitive condition for uniform integrability</span><span class="result-count">2 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If for some $\delta \gt  0$, $\mathbb{E}\lVert Z_n \rVert^{1+\delta} \le C \lt  \infty$, then $Z_n$ is uniformly integrable</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-uniformintegrable-one-of-elpnorm-bdd-gt-one">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.uniformIntegrable_one_of_eLpNorm_bdd_gt_one</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.14, uniform higher-moment UI wrapper.</strong></p>
<p>If the sequence is uniformly bounded in <code>Lᵖ</code> for some finite exponent <code>p &gt; 1</code>,
then it is uniformly integrable in <code>L¹</code>. This is the broader textbook
sufficient condition behind the iid finite-first-moment face above. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {Z : Nat → Ω → Real} {p : ENNReal},
  ENNReal.instPartialOrder.lt 1 p →
    Ne p instTopENNReal.top →
      (∀ (i : Nat), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (Z i) μ) →
        (Exists fun B =&gt;
            ∀ (i : Nat), ENNReal.instPartialOrder.le (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (Z i) p μ) (ENNReal.ofNNReal B)) →
          MeasureTheory.UniformIntegrable Z 1 μ</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean#L267">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean:267</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-uniformintegrable-one-of-identdistrib-memlp">

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.14, identically distributed <code>L¹</code> UI wrapper.</strong></p>
<p>An identically distributed real sequence with a finite first moment is uniformly

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-15-convergence-of-moments-under-uniform-integrability">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.15 convergence of moments under uniform integrability</span><span class="result-count">2 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $Z_n \xrightarrow{d} Z$ and $Z_n$ is uniformly integrable, then $\mathbb{E}[Z_n] \to \mathbb{E}[Z]$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendstoindistribution-integral-tendsto-of-uniformintegrable">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.TendstoInDistribution.integral_tendsto_of_uniformIntegrable</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.15, weak-convergence UI moment wrapper.</strong></p>
<p>If <code>Xₙ ⇒ Z</code> and the source sequence is uniformly integrable in <code>L¹</code>, then the
real expectations converge.  The proof derives the explicit clipping-tail
premise from Mathlib's <code>UniformIntegrable</code> tail characterization and the
limit-law integrability supplied by the bounded-first-moment weak-convergence
wrapper above. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_4} {Ω&#x27; : Type u_5} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩ&#x27; : MeasurableSpace Ω&#x27;} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [inst : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω&#x27;}
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] {X : Nat → Ω → Real} {Z : Ω&#x27; → Real},
  MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution X Filter.atTop Z (fun x =&gt; μ) ν →
    MeasureTheory.UniformIntegrable X 1 μ →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n =&gt; MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt; X n ω) Filter.atTop
        (nhds (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ω =&gt; Z ω))</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean#L1113">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean:1113</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendsto-integral-of-tendstoinmeasure-uniformintegrable">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.tendsto_integral_of_tendstoInMeasure_uniformIntegrable</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.15, convergence-in-measure UI moment wrapper.</strong></p>
<p>If real random variables are uniformly integrable and converge in measure, then
their expectations converge. This is the Vitali/convergence-in-measure face of
Hansen's moment-convergence theorem; the textbook weak-convergence version has a
stronger mode-of-convergence premise than this wrapper exposes. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {α : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {Z : Nat → α → Real} {Zlim : α → Real},
  MeasureTheory.UniformIntegrable Z 1 μ →
    MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ Z Filter.atTop Zlim →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n =&gt; MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt; Z n ω) Filter.atTop
        (nhds (MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt; Zlim ω))</code></pre>
</details>

</div>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-6-16-uniform-stochastic-bounds-for-maxima">
<summary><span>Theorem 6.16 uniform stochastic bounds for maxima</span><span class="result-count">5 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $\lvert Y_i \rvert^r$ is uniformly integrable, then $n^{-1/r} \max_{1 \le i \le n} \lvert Y_i \rvert \xrightarrow{p} 0$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-maxnnnorm">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">def</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.maxNNNorm</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Finite-sample maximum of the norms of a real-valued sequence. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">{Ω : Type u_1} → (Nat → Ω → Real) → Nat → Ω → NNReal</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean#L22">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean:22</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-scaledmaxnnnorm">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">def</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.scaledMaxNNNorm</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Power-scale version of Hansen's maximum statistic.</p>
<p>When <code>Z i = |Y i| ^ r</code>, this is <code>n⁻¹ max_i |Y_i|^r</code>, the natural
nonnegative-power form of Theorem 6.16 before applying the <code>r</code>th-root CMT. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">{Ω : Type u_1} → (Nat → Ω → Real) → Nat → Ω → Real</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean#L29">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean:29</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-max-norm-scaled-tendstoinmeasure-zero-of-uniformintegrable-norm-r">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.max_norm_scaled_tendstoInMeasure_zero_of_uniformIntegrable_norm_r</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 6.16 on the nonnegative power scale.</p>
<p>If <code>Z_i = |Y_i|^r</code> is uniformly integrable in <code>L¹</code>, then
<code>n⁻¹ max_{i&lt;n} |Y_i|^r</code> converges to zero in measure.  The textbook
<code>n^{-1/r} max_i |Y_i|</code> form follows by applying the <code>r</code>th-root continuous
mapping theorem to this nonnegative statistic. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Z : Nat → Ω → Real},
  MeasureTheory.UniformIntegrable Z 1 μ →
    MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.scaledMaxNNNorm Z) Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; 0</code></pre>
</details>
<details class="dependency-list"><summary>Direct statement dependencies (1)</summary><ul><li><code>HansenEconometrics.scaledMaxNNNorm</code></li></ul></details>
<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean#L222">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils/MaxBounds.lean:222</a></p>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-max-norm-scaled-tendstoinmeasure-zero-of-identdistrib-memlp">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.max_norm_scaled_tendstoInMeasure_zero_of_identDistrib_memLp</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 6.16, iid finite-power-moment maximum wrapper.</strong></p>
<p>If the power variables <code>Z_i</code> are identically distributed and <code>Z_0</code> is in <code>L¹</code>,
then <code>n⁻¹ max_{i&lt;n} |Z_i|</code> on the nonnegative-power scale is <code>oₚ(1)</code>.
For Hansen's textbook statement, use <code>Z_i = |Y_i|^r</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {Z : Nat → Ω → Real},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp (Z 0) 1 μ →
    (∀ (i : Nat), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z i) (Z 0) μ μ) →
      MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.scaledMaxNNNorm Z) Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; 0</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendstoinmeasure-sqrt-nonneg-zero-real">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.TendstoInMeasure.sqrt_nonneg_zero_real</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Square-root continuous mapping at zero for nonnegative real-valued sequences.</p>
<p>This avoids any additional measurability side condition by comparing the tail
events <code>{sqrt Xₙ ≥ ε}</code> and <code>{Xₙ ≥ ε²}</code> directly. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {α : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {X : Nat → α → Real},
  (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ X Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; 0) →
    (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : α), Real.instLE.le 0 (X n ω)) →
      MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n ω =&gt; (X n ω).sqrt) Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; 0</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean#L1219">HansenEconometrics/AsymptoticUtils.lean:1219</a></p>
</div>
